details: The US August Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index increased by a cooler-than-expected 0.2% month-over-month. This softer inflation reading has reduced the urgency for the Federal Reserve to implement another interest rate hike in October, a sentiment echoed by New York Fed President John Williams. Bitcoin reacted positively to this news, surging above $85,000. While some Fed officials still suggest further rate adjustments are likely due to persistent inflation, the immediate pressure for an October hike has lessened.
title: US Inflation Data Eases Rate Hike Concerns, Boosts Bitcoin

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has launched an innovation program for the digital euro, inviting fintechs and payment firms to explore applications of AI and crypto technologies in future payment systems. The initiative will conduct testing from January to June 2027, focusing on features like electronic receipts, multi-party transactions, and machine-to-machine payments. While this signifies central bank interest in advanced payment technologies, some critics express concerns about potential state control and privacy implications compared to decentralized cryptocurrencies, and the digital euro could pose competition for private stablecoins.
title: ECB Explores AI & Crypto Use Cases for Digital Euro

details: An unexpectedly robust US August jobs report, released earlier in the week, initially led to Bitcoin's price falling below $80,000. Strong employment figures typically suggest that the economy can sustain inflationary pressures, potentially prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain a hawkish monetary policy or consider further interest rate hikes. This outlook generally weighs on speculative assets like cryptocurrencies, as higher interest rates increase the attractiveness of traditional, yield-bearing assets.
title: Strong US Jobs Report Initially Pressured Bitcoin Below $80K

details: Bitcoin's effectiveness as a short-term inflation hedge is facing scrutiny, particularly in the context of the Federal Reserve's recent interest rate hike and the subsequent rise in Treasury yields. While Bitcoin's limited supply offers a long-term defense against currency devaluation, its recent price movements indicate it behaves more like a speculative asset. Higher bond yields present a competitive alternative, offering steady returns that can draw capital away from non-yielding assets like Bitcoin in a tightening monetary environment.
title: Bitcoin's Inflation Hedge Role Questioned Amidst Rising Yields

details: China's Ministry of State Security has intensified its crackdown on cryptocurrencies by labeling them an "accomplice" to espionage. This move reinforces the nation's 2026 regulations, which strictly prohibit crypto trading and domestic real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. The government cites concerns over economic and financial stability, national security, and property rights as justifications for its stringent stance, contrasting sharply with more open approaches to digital assets in other jurisdictions like Hong Kong.
title: China Reinforces Crypto Ban, Citing Espionage Risks
